title: White Horde
capsule: The White Horde was the eastern wing of the Jochid ulus, the Mongol successor state deriving from Batu Khan's elder brother Orda Khan, whose pasturelands stretched from western Siberia to the lower Syr Darya. For much of the 13th and 14th centuries the White Horde operated as a junior but distinct entity from the Golden Horde ruling the Pontic steppe, largely subordinated yet maintaining its own khans. From c. 1369 Urus Khan consolidated control and reasserted independence, but the polity was transformed when Tokhtamysh, backed by Timur, seized the White Horde's resources and used them as a base to reunify the entire Jochid domain under his authority by the early 1380s, effectively absorbing the White Horde into the reunited Golden Horde.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. White Horde territorial extent is highly conjectural; steppe polities of this type lacked fixed administrative boundaries, and the geometry is reconstructed from Mongol genealogical sources and Persian chronicles with wide uncertainty margins, particularly in the north and east.
